overall: The AG found the Brockton Water Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by holding an unlawful August 30, 2010 executive session with inadequate notice and no minutes, but found no intentional violation.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the Commission did not give proper notice of why the August 30, 2010 meeting was called, including the executive session purpose.
allegations.key_passage: The August 27, 2010 revised meeting notice was not posted sufficiently in advance of the August 30, 2010 meeting to comply with the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: The revised notice listed only 'Section 21(A)(1)' as the executive session topic, and the original notice said only 'Executive Session'.
allegations.key_passage: Moreover, the revised notice's mere listing of "Section 21(A)(1)" as the topic for the executive session was not sufficiently specific to comply with the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the Commission did not follow the required procedures for entering executive session under Purpose One, including the chair's reconvene/adjourn announcement.
allegations.key_passage: From the evidence reviewed, it appears that the Commission did not provide an adequate statement of the purpose for entering executive session, and failed to list a purpose in the minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the Commission cited no allowable purpose; the session was held to discuss media strategy and press conduct, which Purpose One does not cover.
allegations.key_passage: There is no provision in the Open Meeting Law that allows a public body to discuss media strategy in executive session.

allegations.summary: The Commission recorded the hour-long executive session on a mini-cassette but created no written minutes and no record of votes.
allegations.key_passage: Here, while the Commission recorded the executive session, it failed to create any written minutes of the hour-long discussion.

allegations.summary: Complainants requested a finding that the violations were intentional.
allegations.key_passage: We do not find that the Commission members acted with intent to violate the Open Meeting Law, but find their lack of attention to the law in the face of a clear warning to be a serious error of judgment.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

Attend a training on the Open Meeting Law, if the members have not done so since the complaints were filed, and certify to this Office that every member of the Commission has attended such a training.
Create and publicly release minutes, including a detailed summary of the discussion, for the August 30, 2010 executive session.
Consult with and receive approval by the City Solicitor before entering any executive session for two calendar years, beginning on the date of this letter.
remedy_passage: Create and publicly release minutes, including a detailed summary of the discussion, for the August 30, 2010 executive session.
